writeup: TIC 114549849 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 21.72 percent and an orbital period of 8.6790 days. A secondary eclipse was also detected at 7.7 sigma significance, located at phase -0.41. The binary signal achieved a detection significance of 286.0 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise ratio of 54.6 and a centroid offset of 2.0 arcseconds from the target. This candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.55 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine physical system.
